review_notes: I read the whole target file and searched the algebraic-groups library for repeated proof blocks. The strongest case is the Laurent-coordinate extensionality lemma. It is proved four times with the same argument, once in this file and three times in sibling files. I checked that Multiplicative.lean, which the target imports transitively, has no public version. The other candidates are the point-level proof `diagonalGroupProjection_point` and the global-unit proof `diagonalGroupProjection_globalUnit`, and the `Fin 0` and `PEmpty` terminality defs. I did not report these: the first pair share only short rewriting steps, and the terminality defs are thin wrappers. I did not compile the proposed replacement. The existing `simpa` closing steps may need small adjustment after the move into Multiplicative.lean, but the hypotheses and imports are identical in all four copies.

findings.problem: This private lemma says that two K-algebra maps out of the Laurent coordinate ring `multiplicativeGroupCoordinateRing K` agree if they agree on `multiplicativeGroupCoordinate K`. Its proof is a nontrivial argument: transport both maps through `multiplicativeGroupMulEquivAlgHom` to units, compare with `Units.ext` and `multiplicativeGroupMulEquivAlgHom_coordinate`, then transport back. The same statement and the same proof are repeated verbatim, with only variable names changed, in three other files: `generalLinearDeterminant_coordinate_ext`, `generalLinearSection_laurent_ext` and `laurentCoordinateHom_ext`. Each copy is private, so none can be reused. The argument concerns only `multiplicativeGroupCoordinateRing`, so it belongs next to `multiplicativeGroupMulEquivAlgHom_coordinate` in Multiplicative.lean. Any later file that needs this extensionality will copy it a fifth time.
findings.proposed_change: In `AlgebraicGroups/GroupScheme/Multiplicative.lean`, right after `multiplicativeGroupMulEquivAlgHom_coordinate`, add one public lemma, e.g. `theorem multiplicativeGroupCoordinateRing_algHom_ext (K : Type u) [CommRing K] {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra K R] {f g : multiplicativeGroupCoordinateRing K →ₐ[K] R} (h : f (multiplicativeGroupCoordinate K) = g (multiplicativeGroupCoordinate K)) : f = g`. The proof is the existing one: set `e := multiplicativeGroupMulEquivAlgHom K R`, show `e.symm (toConv f) = e.symm (toConv g)` by `Units.ext` plus `multiplicativeGroupMulEquivAlgHom_coordinate` and `h`, then apply `e` and `ofConv`. The `@[ext]` attribute can be added. Then delete the four private copies. In this file delete `diagonalGroupLaurent_ext` and replace its four uses with the shared lemma: `apply multiplicativeGroupCoordinateRing_algHom_ext K` in `diagonalGroupProjectionBialgHom` (both bullets, lines 110 and 117) and in `diagonalGroupProjection_point` (line 144). The hypotheses are unchanged, since `K : Type u` and `R : Type u` as before. In GeneralLinearDeterminant.lean, GeneralLinearDeterminantSection.lean and SpecialLinearKernel.lean, replace the respective `*_ext` / `laurentCoordinateHom_ext` call sites the same way. All of them already import Multiplicative.lean, directly or through Diagonal, GeneralLinear or SpecialLinear.
findings.benefit: The unit-transport argument is stated and maintained once instead of four times. A change to `multiplicativeGroupMulEquivAlgHom` then needs one proof update. The four files each lose about 14 lines of boilerplate, and readers no longer wonder whether the near-identical private lemmas differ in some subtle way. Future Laurent-coordinate proofs can reuse a named public lemma.
